samples.question: The picture shows a plain background covered with many small dark dots and one red cross. The dots come in close pairs: every dot has exactly one partner much nearer to it than any other dot, so each pair is a short two-dot segment. For each pair compare the direction of its own two-dot segment with the direction from the red cross to that pair. Every pair follows the same rule, up to a small random wobble. If the pairs point along the direction to the red cross the pattern is radial; if they point at right angles to that direction the pattern is circular; if they point about halfway between those two, near forty-five degrees, the pattern is spiral. Colour, dot size, pair length, the number of pairs and the position of the cross carry no information. Is the pattern radial, spiral or circular? Answer radial, spiral or circular.
